detail: The counter startup-memory-tokens is read by the daily growth check, but no transition of the session changes it: the three memory files grow by edits that the cited text assigns to curation and to the captain, not to a session transition. The model therefore declares the counter with no changing transition.

subject: c1
c9
detail: Crash survival rests on two read facts: the session lock goes stale when its owning pid dies (c9), and the agent is told to rebuild from durable records after a restart (c1). The pinned text gives no account of what happens to a tool call or a git operation that a crash cuts in half, other than the per-script rollbacks of the lock sidecar. No source says how long a home may stay without a session, and none was observed.

subject: c27

detail: The pinned text gives no measure of how a long session degrades. It names compaction as losing the digest (c27) and caps the startup memory by estimated tokens (c29), but states no limit on the length of one session, on conversation size, or on the number of turns, and no staleness check on a running agent's context other than the digest re-emit and the growth check. Context rot is therefore recorded here as a gap, not described as a mechanism.

subject: c36
c35
detail: For unattended operation on a platform other than macOS, the alert channel for a stalled away-mode injection defaults to none (c36), and the away record sets no deadline after which a held captain decision is made without the captain (c35). The pinned text does not say how a captain on such a platform learns of a stall unless a command channel is configured.

detail: Drift between the running agent and the shared instructions is handled by the update path only when the captain triggers it (c42). The pinned text names no scheduled update and no check that a long-running agent's loaded instructions still match the files on disk. A skipped home stays on old bytes until a later pass surfaces its record (c45, c46).
